description: Todo-marker enrichment: has_todo, todo_count, todo_tags (sorted unique TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX). Grounded on three corpora: forgeql-pub.frozen for Rust source markers, C/C++ fixture patterns and the corpus that must NOT move; pytorch-andre.pytorch-frozen for the leading position, where a marker comment opening a Python body is a sibling of the body block rather than a child of it; and zephyr-andre.frozen for the partition that says which grammar the gain came from.

cases.name: todo_in_cpp_fixture
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'tests/fixtures/enrichment_patterns.cpp' WHERE fql_kind='function' WHERE has_todo='true' WHERE name MATCHES '^todo' ORDER BY line ASC LIMIT 10

cases.name: todo_count_rust
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'crates/forgeql-core/src/ast/enrich/todo.rs' WHERE fql_kind='function' WHERE name='marker_word_boundary' WHERE todo_count=3 LIMIT 5

cases.name: todo_tags_multi_marker
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind='function' WHERE has_todo='true' WHERE todo_tags='FIXME,HACK,TODO' ORDER BY line ASC LIMIT 10

cases.name: negative_no_todo_in_rust
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'crates/forgeql-core/src/node_id.rs' WHERE fql_kind='function' WHERE has_todo='true' LIMIT 5

cases.name: control_the_frozen_snapshot_did_not_move
cases.description: The other side of the fix, and the reason it is a control rather than an afterthought: the corpora that DID move cannot tell a correct widening from one that started counting comments it has no business counting; only a corpus that must not move can. This snapshot must not, and the claim is about the SNAPSHOT, not about the working tree — the commit adds fixture files carrying markers in both new positions, and those are not in it. Be exact about what it therefore controls: the snapshot holds no Python at all, so it cannot exercise the leading position; what it holds at rest is the OTHER position the fix opens, a marker between a signature and a body, across its C, C++ and Rust. The count stays at exactly 9 — measured live on 0.190.0, the pre-fix binary, against this same snapshot on 2026-08-26.

cases.name: the_zephyr_gain_is_all_in_its_python
cases.description: Where the seven rows this corpus gained actually came from. Its corpus-wide count is pinned at 958 in open_defects.json, 951 before the fix; that number alone does not say which grammar moved, and the fix opens a position in brace-delimited grammars too, so on a corpus that is overwhelmingly C the natural reading could be wrong. Partitioning it settles the attribution: 44 Python functions answer now against 37 before — the 37 measured live on 0.190.0 against this same frozen snapshot, 2026-08-26, before the fix was built — which accounts for all seven and leaves the C at rest.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE has_todo = 'true' IN '**/*.py' LIMIT 1

cases.name: control_a_todo_after_a_statement_is_found
cases.description: Anchors the leading-position case below by ruling out the two explanations that are not the defect: `cat` is decorated too, and it sits in the same file, so neither decoration nor the file is why the marker was missed. Its body opens with a nested `def`, so its TODO was never the first thing in the body and it answered all along.
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'torch/_refs/__init__.py' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE line = 2878 WHERE has_todo = 'true' LIMIT 2

cases.name: control_the_leading_todo_is_still_on_line_4818
cases.description: Anchors the case's identity rather than only its row: it is addressed by line against a frozen snapshot, so a re-pin that shifted the file could turn it green while proving nothing.
cases.fql: SHOW LINES 4818-4818 OF 'torch/_refs/__init__.py' WHERE text MATCHES 'TODO'

cases.name: control_the_function_holding_it_is_indexed
cases.description: And that the function whose body it opens is a row at all, so the case below can only fail on the marker.
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'torch/_refs/__init__.py' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE line = 4816 LIMIT 2

cases.name: a_todo_on_the_first_body_line_is_found
cases.description: A marker comment that is the FIRST thing in a function body is counted. `t` opens with `# TODO: Add sparse support` and answered no has_todo at all, because the scan walked the body subtree only and tree-sitter-python does not open the block until the first statement — the comment is parsed as a sibling of the block. The count and the tags are pinned beside the row, not just its presence: the scan now visits the function node as well as its body, and a grammar that had the comment inside the body all along would report this marker twice.
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'torch/_refs/__init__.py' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE line = 4816 WHERE has_todo = 'true' WHERE todo_count = 1 WHERE todo_tags = 'TODO' LIMIT 2

cases.name: the_file_gained_the_functions_that_open_with_a_marker
cases.description: Breadth beside the single row: one named function proves the position is reachable, not that the fix reaches every function in that position. This file answers 12 rows now against 8 before — the 8 measured live on 0.188.0 when this defect was filed and confirmed by the gate run that moved this case's own assert from 8 to 12 — and the number is what says the correction landed across the file rather than on the row a test happened to name.
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'torch/_refs/__init__.py' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE has_todo = 'true' LIMIT 40
